kind: registration: the census questions, the cap ladder and the decision rule, before any count
question: Why can the mean form not fit the residue of `lane-scalefit`'s census -- the genes 7d excluded as basal_not_positive whose summed single-removal drops STILL reach or exceed the gene's whole intact level after every drop is multiplied by M2h's fixed 0.2146 -- and is the excess carried by one or a few elements, or spread across many? The answer decides what the next combination form should be: a PER-ELEMENT CAP if one or a few elements dominate, something else if the sum is diffuse.
population: RE-DERIVED, not copied. The 24 compiled non-coding programs are gated and parsed again with 7d's own code (`combine2.multi_rule_genes`, `combine2.gene_rules`, `combine2.classify`, `combine2.fit` at THETA = 0.5 and bridge.H_INTACT = 0.5, selection `combine2.SELECTION`), the mean form's `basal_not_positive` genes are taken from that run, and the RESIDUE is those of them whose fit is still `basal_not_positive` on the scaled observations (`scalefit.scaled_rho`). The count is computed by calling `combine2.fit` twice per gene, exactly as scalefit did, never by the identity q_scaled = SCALE * q. scalefit's committed counts (12,500 excluded and its residue) are read AFTERWARDS and reconciled against this run; a disagreement is a finding of this lane and not something to repair. The RECOVERED population, the excluded genes that are NOT in the residue, is measured beside it in every statistic, because a concentration number means nothing without the population it is contrasted with. The two are never pooled. The promoter-competition form is NOT this lane's population: the mean form is the runtime default and scalefit's primary, and the drop shares below are the mean form's q by construction.
drops: every statistic below is over a gene's ACTIVATING single-removal drops d_i = 1 - RHO_i for RHO_i < 1, and over no other quantity. That is the set `combine2.fit` sums into q under the mean form, so the shares below are shares of exactly the quantity that exceeds the gene's level. An inhibiting element's lift (RHO_j - 1) does not enter q and is not counted in any share; the number of inhibiting elements is recorded per gene as a descriptive column and decides nothing.

questions.Q1_re_derivation: How many genes are in the residue, re-derived from the compiled programs by this lane's own run? Reported with the re-derived count of the excluded population it is a subset of, and reconciled against scalefit's committed numbers after the fact.
questions.Q2_how_many_elements: For each residue gene, the number of elements (rules) and the number of activating elements. Reported as the quantiles 0.01, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.99 and the min, max and mean, over the residue and over the recovered beside it -- the DISTRIBUTIONS, not only the medians.
questions.Q3_share_of_the_largest_element: For each residue gene, top1 = (the largest activating drop) / (the sum of the activating drops): the share of the summed drop carried by its largest single element. Quantiles as in Q2, over the residue and the recovered. This is the statistic that decides the question: a residue whose median top1 is near 1 is a residue of genes with one dominant element; a residue whose median top1 is near 1/n is a residue of genes whose elements all contribute alike.
questions.Q4_share_of_the_largest_three: The same for top3 = (the sum of the three largest activating drops) / (the sum of all of them), which is 1 for a gene with three or fewer activating elements. Quantiles as in Q2, over both populations, and separately over the residue genes with four or more activating elements, for which the number is not forced to 1.
questions.Q5_ratio_after_scaling: For each residue gene, the ratio after scaling, q_after = SCALE * (sum of the activating drops), which is the mean form's q on the scaled observations. All residue genes are at or above 1 by construction, so what the quantiles say is HOW FAR above: a residue sitting just above 1 is a different problem from one sitting at 5. Quantiles as in Q2, plus the count at or above 2 and at or above 5. The unscaled ratio's quantiles are reported beside it.
questions.Q6_how_few_elements_carry_the_excess: For each residue gene, k_min = the smallest number of its LARGEST activating drops whose removal from the sum would bring the scaled sum of the rest below 1, i.e. the smallest k with SCALE * (sum of all drops - the k largest) < 1; and NaN if no k < n achieves it (a gene whose drops cannot be brought under the level by dropping all but one). Quantiles as in Q2, and the counts at k_min = 1, = 2, = 3, <= 3 and > 3. REMOVING an element is not a form this lane proposes and not a fit: it is a concentration statistic, the direct reading of 'carried by one or a few'.
questions.Q7_recovery_under_a_per_element_cap: Under a PER-ELEMENT CAP at level L, how many residue genes get a positive basal rate back? The cap rule, the ladder of L, and the arithmetic bound on what a cap can do are in CAP_RULE, CAP_LEVELS and CAP_BOUND below, all declared before the count. Reported as the count and share recovered at EVERY L of the ladder -- the whole curve, not a chosen point -- with the primary L named in advance.
questions.Q8_diffuseness: For each residue gene, n_eff = (sum of the drops)^2 / (sum of the drops squared), the inverse Herfindahl index of the drop shares: the effective number of elements the summed drop is spread over, which is 1 when one element carries all of it and n when all n contribute equally. Also n_eff / n_activating. Quantiles as in Q2, over both populations. This is Q3 and Q4's statistic read on the whole vector rather than its head, and it is declared so that a flat top1 cannot be reported as concentration or a peaked one as diffusion.

cap_rule: A per-element cap at level L replaces every scaled activating drop by min(SCALE * d_i, L) and leaves the inhibiting lifts untouched. The gene has a positive basal rate again -- it becomes fittable at the step 7d excluded it on -- exactly when the capped sum is below 1. L is in units of the gene's INTACT LEVEL, which is the unit q is already in, so L = 0.1 reads 'no single element may claim more than a tenth of the gene'. Capping is applied on top of M2h's scale and never instead of it, and the count is computed by summing the capped drops, with `combine2.fit` called on the capped observations as a cross-check on every gene.
cap_levels_reason: Seven round levels -- halves and decades -- spanning two orders of magnitude, from the whole of the gene's level down to a hundredth of it, fixed in this file before a single gene was counted. THE WHOLE CURVE IS REPORTED AND NO LEVEL IS SELECTED AFTERWARDS, because a cap chosen after seeing the distribution is a fitted parameter wearing a census's clothes: it would be the one number that makes the count come out well, reported as though it had been a prediction. The ladder is round decades and halves precisely so that it cannot have been tuned -- there is no free digit in it. The PRIMARY level is 0.5, for a reason about the model and not about the data: an element may claim at most half of the gene's intact level, which is the same half the engine already uses as bridge.H_INTACT = 0.5 and combine2.THETA = 0.5, and it is the weakest cap that forces a multi-element gene's level to be shared. The primary decides the WORDING of Q7, never the verdict on the question, which is decided by Q3, Q4, Q6 and Q8 through DECISION_RULE.
cap_bound: Stated in advance, from the algebra: a cap at L leaves the capped sum at most n_activating * L, so a cap at L CANNOT fit any gene with n_activating >= 1/L, and it fits EVERY gene with n_activating < 1/L whatever its drops are. L = 1.0 and L = 0.5 therefore recover at most the residue genes with one activating element -- of which there are none, the population being multi-element and the drops summing above 4.66 -- unless a gene's capped sum falls below 1 some other way, so the top of the ladder is expected to be near zero and its being zero is not a finding. The bound is the reason the ladder runs down two decades: the count must be able to go from nothing to nearly everything inside it for the curve to say anything, and 1/0.01 = 100 sits above the rule counts scalefit published for the residue (see PRIOR_EXPOSURE). A cap also destroys the bridge's exact-reproduction principle further than the scale already does: a capped element's run reproduces neither its own removal observation nor 0.2146 of it. THIS LANE PROPOSES NO FORM; it counts what a cap could and could not do, and stops.
decision_rule: Decided on the RESIDUE's medians, in this order, with the thresholds fixed here before the count. CONCENTRATED, if the median top1 >= 0.5: the largest single element carries most of the summed drop, and a per-element cap is the indicated next form. FEW, if the median top3 >= 0.75 or the median k_min <= 3: no one element dominates but three do, and a correction on a few elements per gene -- of which a cap is one -- can reach the residue. DIFFUSE, if the median top1 < 0.25 AND the median k_min > 3: what exceeds the gene is the sum over many comparable elements, no element is the culprit, and a per-element cap is NOT the indicated form. MIXED otherwise, reported as mixed and not rounded to either side. The thresholds are the plain readings of the words: a half is 'most of', a largest-of-three at three quarters is 'a few carry it', a quarter is 'the largest carries little', and three is the brief's own 'one or a few'. Q7's curve is reported in every case and changes no branch of this rule.

readings.concentrated: the excess is CARRIED BY ONE ELEMENT: over the residue the median gene's largest activating single-removal drop is at least half of its summed drop, so what exceeds the gene's level is one element's size and not the number of elements. A PER-ELEMENT CAP is the indicated next combination form.
readings.few: the excess is CARRIED BY A FEW ELEMENTS: no single element carries most of the residue gene's summed drop, but its three largest do, or removing at most three of them would bring the sum under the gene's level. A correction that acts on a few elements per gene, of which a per-element cap is one, can reach the residue.
readings.diffuse: the excess is SPREAD ACROSS MANY ELEMENTS: over the residue the median gene's largest activating drop is under a quarter of its summed drop and more than three elements would have to be removed to bring the sum under the gene's level. What exceeds the gene is the SUM over many comparable elements, no element is the culprit, and a per-element cap is NOT the indicated next form.
readings.mixed: the excess is NEITHER clearly concentrated nor clearly diffuse by the thresholds declared before the count: the residue's medians fall between them. Reported as mixed and not rounded to either side; what the next form should be is not decided by this census.

to_be_reconciled_against.used_as: the target of a reconciliation performed AFTER this lane's own count. The census re-derives every number from the 24 compiled programs with combine2's own code and never reads these

prior_exposure: Disclosed, because it was read before these questions were written. scalefit's committed census (`7f65544`, data/results/scalefit_census.json) already publishes, for the residue, the RULE-COUNT quantiles 0.25 41, median 58, 0.75 84, 0.99 194, against 0.25 10, median 15, 0.75 23 for the recovered, and its commit message argues from them that 'summing per-element maxima over many elements -- not the magnitude of any one element -- is what exceeds the gene'. So Q2's answer is ALREADY KNOWN in outline and Q2 is a re-derivation and not a test, and the DIFFUSE branch of DECISION_RULE is the branch that prior reading points at. What is NOT known from it, and is what this lane measures, is how the summed drop is distributed WITHIN a gene: a gene with 58 elements can still have one element carrying 90% of the sum, and the published rule counts say nothing either way. Q3, Q4, Q6, Q7 and Q8 have no published precedent that this lane is aware of. The thresholds and the cap ladder were nevertheless chosen to be round and symmetric rather than tuned to make the expected branch come out, and the ladder's lower end was set at 0.01 because 1/0.01 = 100 clears the published 0.99 rule count of 194 only partly -- a level chosen to be round, not to be flattering.
what_this_lane_does_not_do: it proposes NO combination form, registers NO RNA test, and makes NO claim about expression. A gene a fit can accept is not a gene the model predicts: lane-recovered (f775e9b) had to establish that separately for the genes that recovered at the scale, and nothing here inherits its reading. Q7 counts what a per-element cap could do to the arithmetic and stops there; whether a cap belongs in the engine is another lane's registration
limitations: the residue is defined by M2h's scale for the MULTIPLICATIVE composition, transferred to the mean form. M2h's own mean scale read +0.05032, at which the threshold would be 19.9 instead of 4.66 and the residue would be much smaller. The transfer is scalefit's registered choice and this lane inherits it unchanged rather than re-opening it; every count here is conditional on it

fittable is not predicted. Every count in this census is about whether 7d's fit has a positive basal rate left, which is a property of the arithmetic. Whether any of these genes would then read closer to measured RNA is a SEPARATE registration on separate data, as `lane-recovered` had to be for the genes that recovered at the scale alone. NO RNA VALUE IS OPENED IN THIS LANE AND NO EXPRESSION CLAIM IS MADE

a cap is counted, not proposed. Q7 measures what a per-element cap could do to the residue's arithmetic. It does not say a cap is right, it does not say the capped drops are the drops the bridge observed -- they are not -- and this lane registers no form and no test of one

the shares are of the compiled drops, which are themselves predicted rules carrying whatever error the compilation carries. A concentration measured on wrong drops is a concentration of the wrong drops. This census measures the predictor as it stands and nothing behind it
k_min and n_eff are concentration statistics computed on one gene at a time. Neither is a model, and neither licenses deleting or reweighting any element in any run
stop_list_check: docs/ROADMAP.md §5, 'The stop list of 2026-09-27, reinstated': this lane touches no stop item. No AlphaGenome request and no deletion request, no new reader biosample, nothing in area J, no node-model work, no BioForge calibration
money: none: no request is sent and no key is read

exclusions: no gene is excluded here: this record declares the questions and computes no count
result_manifest.partitions: n/a: a registration for a predictor-side census; no outcome read and no RNA opened

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 86c8ab4

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
